back: A diarrhoeal disease caused by the bacterium Vibrio cholerae, spread by the faecal–oral route through contaminated water and food; dehydration can kill within hours if untreated.
Oral rehydration solution for most patients, drips for severe cases and antibiotics for severe cases; case fatality should be under 1% with prompt treatment.
No safe water or sanitation, poverty, crowding (informal settlements, camps), floods and cyclones, poor hygiene and delayed access to treatment.
WHO estimates about 1.3 to 4 million cases and 21 000 to 143 000 deaths a year; endemic in parts of South Asia and Africa.
Nearly 100 000 cases and over 4 000 deaths (WHO, rounded); began in the high-density suburbs of Harare and Chitungwiza after water and sewage systems failed.
Safe water (chlorination, boreholes), sanitation (latrines, sewers), handwashing and food hygiene, education, oral cholera vaccine in outbreaks, surveillance and rapid response.
Deaths among cases ÷ number of cases × 100.
Floods and cyclones contaminate water, damage pipes and sewers and crowd people into shelters; cases were confirmed in Beira after Cyclone Idai (2019) and in Haiti after the 2010 earthquake.
